A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TT-SPARSE research. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original predictive-performance and complexity results on 28 datasets in Tables 1–3, alongside component and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds operator measurements, sparsification comparisons, per-node complexity analyses, and synthetic and tabular expressivity experiments.

M1.justification: Appendix I introduces an auxiliary Deep LTT variant with a ReLU hidden path, default width 2^k, and a linear residual path sharing the TopK mask. The standard TT-SPARSE architecture, routing, pruning, and extraction procedures remain unchanged; expanded gradient explanations largely restate v1 Appendix D.

E1.justification: The original 28-dataset inventory and three tabular task types remain unchanged. v2 adds exhaustive fitting of all 256 three-bit Boolean functions, a distinct synthetic expressivity task. Its four-dataset sparsification study and 27-dataset Deep LTT comparison use existing tabular coverage.

E2.justification: The headline benchmark comparator sets are unchanged. v2 substantially expands component comparisons by evaluating Sinkhorn and Perturbed TopK operators in Table 1, FC + L0 gates, FC + L1 + Prune, and Magnitude TopK in Table 6, and Deep LTT in Appendix I.

E3.justification: v2 adds a GPU/float32/batch-64 operator benchmark averaged across ten configurations, regularization sweeps with a shared QMC extraction pipeline and extractability-based comparison, and exhaustive Boolean-function fitting. These substantially extend evaluation design. The original holdout/validation splits and predictive metrics remain unchanged; newly disclosed training details do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 retains the original Softmax, encoding, fan-in, node-count, temperature, and skip-connection ablations. It adds operator cost/noise diagnostics, per-node complexity with and without don't-care terms, tests of structural sparsity and learned routing, and standard-versus-deep expressivity analyses in Section 4.1 and Appendices H.1–I.

E5.justification: The new operator comparison reports gradient variance and loss standard deviation, with Perturbed results distinguished by 32 versus 256 Monte Carlo samples. The existing five-seed benchmark protocol, standard-error reporting, and Friedman-rank reporting remain unchanged; no increase in benchmark repetitions is established.

E6.justification: All values in v1 Tables 1–3 match v2 Tables 3–5. Substantial new results include operator costs, sparsification outcomes, reduction from 19.24 to 7.13 mean literals with don't-care terms at k=6, and 100% versus 40.6% Boolean-function fit rates for deep versus standard nodes. Standard LTT wins on 24/27 tabular datasets. These are added comparisons, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: v2 adds a Sperner-based bound on threshold-node prime implicants and explicit characterization of standard versus deep-node expressivity. It corrects Figure 4's inconsistent weights and Boolean formula. The Soft TopK optimization and gradient derivations retain their substance, with notation and indexing refinements.

C1.justification: The central claims about sparse differentiable routing, exact rule extraction, and performance-complexity tradeoffs remain. The introduction and contributions additionally claim zero operator-gradient variance and that TT-SPARSE uniquely supports all three task types natively within one interpretable rule-learning architecture.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges the standard node's linear-separability restriction and interprets the Deep LTT findings as evidence for beneficial regularization. It also adds substantive explanations concerning post-hoc sparsification failures, separate mapping weights, don't-care simplification, and operator memory/noise costs. These considerably expand the explanation and qualification of the design.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies quantile-based thermometer encoding, categorical one-hot encoding, Adam learning rates, batch size, and early stopping. v2 also states training losses, revises the CPU/RAM description from i7/16 GB to dual Xeon/128 GB, and replaces anonymous code-access information with a named GitHub repository. These materially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for straight-through estimation, DILP, L0 regularization, threshold logic, and interpretable clinical prediction, and introduces the claim of unique native support across three task types. The existing related-work categories and most research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 separates Soft TopK and LTT components into numbered subsections, clarifies mathematical terminology, rewrites extraction explanations, consolidates contributions, and condenses experiment and future-work prose. It also adds a conflict-of-interest disclosure. The overall narrative sequence and substantial portions of the text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with operator, node-complexity, sparsification, and Deep LTT tables, plus a new Pareto figure and architecture diagram. Figure 4 is corrected, and several existing illustrations are relocated or rescaled. The original benchmark tables and empirical plot images are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in support for the central design through sparsification controls, operator measurements, and direct testing of the threshold-node expressivity restriction. It also fixes the worked rule-extraction example and supplies essential preprocessing and training details. Figure 17 introduces aggregation and color-label inconsistencies, but these limited defects do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and transparency.
